question.text: What will the month-over-month change in US producer prices excluding food, energy, and trade services be for October 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves based on the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics' Producer Price Index news release for October 2026, scheduled for publication at 8:30 a.m. ET on Friday, November 13, 2026 (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ppi.nr0.htm). The answered value is the seasonally adjusted 1-month percent change reported for the index for "final demand less foods, energy, and trade services" — the figure stated in the release narrative, e.g. "prices for final demand less foods, energy, and trade services moved up 0.5 percent in September." A reported decrease of 0.1 percent resolves as -0.1, and "unchanged" resolves as 0. The value as first published is used; later revisions do not change the resolution.
question.fine_print: If the October 2026 release is delayed, the question resolves when the October 2026 figures are first published. If the October 2026 figures have not been published by February 28, 2027, or if the BLS skips the October 2026 release entirely, the question is annulled.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-15: The latest release, for September 2026, shows the target series, final demand less foods, energy, and trade services, at **+0.5% m/m** (seasonally adjusted). Over the same month, headline final demand rose 1.3%, goods 2.6%, services 0.8%, and transportation and warehousing 3.4%. Data for May through August were revised. [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ppi.nr0.htm)
- 2026-10-15: In the same release, the narrower core (less foods and energy) rose **+0.7% m/m** against a 0.3% consensus, its biggest gain since April. Recent prints for that core: June 0.4% (revised), July 0.3% (revised from 0.2%), August 0.2%. This is a different series from the one the question resolves on. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/core-producer-prices-mom), [ForexFactory](https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/87-us-core-ppi-mm)
- Warning about the statistical baseline you were given: it uses FRED WPSFD4131, which is finished goods less foods and energy. That is not the resolution series, so its percentiles (median about 0.22) are only loosely relevant.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The October figures come out 2026-11-13 at 8:30 a.m. ET. [BLS schedule](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/ppi.htm), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/economic-calendar/core-ppi-735)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02/03: The ISM manufacturing PMI rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5 (consensus 54.6), its 10th straight month of expansion. Production reached 59.0, the fastest since November 2021. Reports mention growing price and supply pressures. S&P Global's manufacturing PMI was 54.9. I did not verify ISM's prices-paid index. [finanznachrichten](https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-11/70009291-u-s-manufacturing-index-increases-more-than-expected-in-october-020.htm), [diariobitcoin](https://www.diariobitcoin.com/estados-unidos/la-manufactura-de-ee-uu-acelera-en-octubre-mientras-crece-la-presion-sobre-los-suministros/)
- 2026-11-01: OPEC+ kept December output unchanged. Brent for December delivery closed at $117.64. [almasryalyoum](https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/4398555)
- 2026-11-02: Crude went above $100 in October and briefly touched $115, driven by attacks on shipping and the Middle East conflict. [oilandgas360](https://www.oilandgas360.com/360-energy-pulse-what-mattered-this-month-in-energy-4/)
- 2026-10-26: The AAA national average for gasoline was $4.27/gal, down from $4.47 a month earlier. That matters for headline PPI and trade margins, but energy and trade are excluded from the target series. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/national-average-falls-6-cents-but-crude-oil-nears-100-barrel/)
- Early October 2026: EIA expected retail diesel to stay above $6/gal through October and then ease gradually. Diesel benchmarks hit record highs (about $220/bbl) in September, and European diesel margins had narrowed by early October. This bears on transportation and warehousing, which is inside the target series. [EnergyNewsBeat](https://energynewsbeat.co/diesel/iea-says-the-diesel-squeeze-lasts-well-into-2027-futures-imply-about-6-diesel-into-january), [devdiscourse](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/business/3988225-us-eia-raises-q4-oil-price-forecast-to-usd-105-amid-middle-east-supply-risks-diesel-market-tightness)
- September 2026, 12-month changes: transportation and warehousing +16.0%, truck freight +19.3%, portfolio management +21.2%. [BLS TED](https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/producer-price-index-up-6-3-percent-in-september-largest-12-month-increase-since-december-2022.htm), [BTS](https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/transportation-producer-price-index-september-2026)
- I could not find October 2026 truck freight rate data from DAT or Cass.

## 4. Base rates
- Recent readings of the target series: July 2026 +0.4, August +0.3, September +0.5. The 12-month rate to September was 5.0% (figures from the question background; September and August confirmed via Trading Economics).
- Over 2023 to 2025, this series usually printed between -0.1 and +0.4, with occasional outliers around ±0.5 to 0.6 (from memory, not verified here). The 2026 regime runs much hotter, at roughly +0.4 a month.
- After big energy-shock months, the transportation and warehousing component often partly reverses. That is a downside risk if diesel eased in October, though it held above $6 by EIA's account. Portfolio management fees follow equity prices with a lag. I did not check October equity performance.
- Typical month-to-month change in the target series is about ±0.2 to 0.3 percentage points.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find a consensus for October on this specific series or for core PPI. The calendar consensus fields are still blank. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/core-producer-prices-mom), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/economic-calendar/core-ppi-735)
- Kalshi, headline PPI m/m for October (prices as of 2026-11-03): above 0.2% at 0.81, above 0.5% at 0.63, above 0.7% at 0.58, above 1.0% at 0.51, above 1.1% at 0.12. Several prices are not monotonic, so the market looks thin. Its implied median is roughly 0.9 to 1.0% on headline. This is not the target series.
- Kalshi, headline PPI y/y for October: implied median about 6.6% (above 6.6% at 0.50), up from 6.3% in September.
- Polymarket's October PPI y/y market shows only about 3% on each of the 5.9% to 6.4% buckets, consistent with expectations above 6.4%.
- Kalshi, October core CPI m/m: 0.2% at 0.41, 0.3% at 0.38.
- No Kalshi or Polymarket market exists for the target series.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around 2026-11-10 to 12: The October CPI release (check the date). Its airline fares and other services may hint at PPI services.
- Before 2026-11-13: The October BTS/Cass freight indexes, EIA weekly diesel prices, and consensus forecasts for core PPI should appear on calendars late in the week of November 9.
- 2026-11-13, 8:30 ET: The PPI release, which resolves the question.

Sources: [BLS PPI release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ppi.nr0.htm), [BLS schedule](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/ppi.htm), [BLS TED](https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/producer-price-index-up-6-3-percent-in-september-largest-12-month-increase-since-december-2022.htm), [BTS](https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/transportation-producer-price-index-september-2026), [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/core-producer-prices-mom), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/economic-calendar/core-ppi-735), [ForexFactory](https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/87-us-core-ppi-mm), [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/national-average-falls-6-cents-but-crude-oil-nears-100-barrel/), [EnergyNewsBeat](https://energynewsbeat.co/diesel/iea-says-the-diesel-squeeze-lasts-well-into-2027-futures-imply-about-6-diesel-into-january), [devdiscourse](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/business/3988225-us-eia-raises-q4-oil-price-forecast-to-usd-105-amid-middle-east-supply-risks-diesel-market-tightness), [finanznachrichten](https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-11/70009291-u-s-manufacturing-index-increases-more-than-expected-in-october-020.htm), [diariobitcoin](https://www.diariobitcoin.com/estados-unidos/la-manufactura-de-ee-uu-acelera-en-octubre-mientras-crece-la-presion-sobre-los-suministros/), [oilandgas360](https://www.oilandgas360.com/360-energy-pulse-what-mattered-this-month-in-energy-4/), [almasryalyoum](https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/4398555)

# Research brief: October 2026 PPI, final demand less foods, energy and trade services (m/m, SA)

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-15: The latest BLS release covers September 2026. Final demand less foods, energy and trade services rose **+0.5%**. Other September figures: headline final demand +1.3%, services +0.8%, transportation and warehousing +3.4%, goods less foods and energy +0.3%. BLS revised its May to August data in the same release. [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ppi.nr0.htm)
- The matching FRED series is WPSFD49116 (seasonally adjusted). The index stood at 144.255 in September 2026, up 5.04% from 137.328 a year earlier. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/WPSFD49116.txt)
- **Warning:** the statistical baseline you were given uses WPSFD4131 (finished goods less foods and energy). That is a different series with lower volatility, so its percentiles (median about 0.22) do not match the resolution series.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The October figure comes out 2026-11-13 at 8:30 ET. Forex Factory confirms that date. [ForexFactory](https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/87-us-core-ppi-mm)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02/03: The ISM manufacturing PMI rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5, beating the 54.6 forecast. Production rose to 59.0, and reports describe supply and price pressures. I could not find the October prices-paid figure. [finanznachrichten](https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-11/70009291-u-s-manufacturing-index-increases-more-than-expected-in-october-020.htm), [diariobitcoin](https://www.diariobitcoin.com/estados-unidos/la-manufactura-de-ee-uu-acelera-en-octubre-mientras-crece-la-presion-sobre-los-suministros/)
- 2026-11-01: OPEC+ kept output unchanged. December Brent closed at $117.64 according to Reuters, as cited by the source. [almasryalyoum](https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/4398555)
- 2026-11-02: Crude went above $100 in October and briefly reached $115, driven by the Middle East conflict and attacks on shipping. Higher diesel and freight costs could push transportation and warehousing services up again. [oilandgas360](https://www.oilandgas360.com/360-energy-pulse-what-mattered-this-month-in-energy-4/)
- 2026-10-26 week: AAA's national gasoline average was $4.27, down from $4.47 a month earlier. Gasoline is excluded from this measure, but it feeds into transport costs. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/national-average-falls-6-cents-but-crude-oil-nears-100-barrel/)
- 2026-10-21: In September, transportation and warehousing was up 16.0% year over year, portfolio management 21.2%, and truck freight 19.3%. [BLS TED](https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/producer-price-index-up-6-3-percent-in-september-largest-12-month-increase-since-december-2022.htm)
- 2026-10-15: Core PPI (excluding food and energy) rose 0.7% against a 0.3% consensus. The ex-food, energy and trade measure beat forecasts too. [ActionForex](https://www.actionforex.com/live-comments/657642-us-ppi-surges-1-3-as-energy-prices-spike-but-core-inflation-also-beats-forecasts/)
- 2026-10-01: ISM prices paid for September was 77.9, up from 71.1 and above the 73.0 estimate. It has been above 70 for eight months in a row. [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/ism-sees-manufacturing-remaining-robust-pushing-up-input-prices)

## 4. Base rates
Monthly changes below are calculated from the current vintage of WPSFD49116, so they include revisions and may differ from first prints. For example, July 2026 was first published as +0.4 and now calculates to +0.5.
- From October 2025 to September 2026: +0.6, +0.3, +0.1, +0.5, +0.5, +0.2, +0.5, +0.8, +0.2, +0.5, +0.3, +0.5.
- **Last 12 months:** mean about 0.41%, standard deviation about 0.18. The range was 0.14 to 0.77, and no month was negative.
- From November 2024 to September 2025: +0.1, +0.3, +0.4, +0.4, +0.1, -0.2, +0.1, +0.1, +0.7, +0.3, +0.2. October 2025 was +0.6.
- **Trend:** the yearly rate rose from about 2.8% in mid-2025 to 5.0% now. Monthly readings in 2026 have run at roughly 0.4% on average.
- Over the last 24 months, about 1 in 24 months was negative, and about 3 in 24 were at or above 0.7.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found **no published consensus** for the October ex-food, energy and trade measure. Trading Economics and Investing.com show the October forecast fields as blank. [TradingEconomics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/core-producer-prices-mom), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/economic-calendar/core-ppi-735)
- Kalshi headline PPI m/m for October (as of 2026-11-03), a related market rather than this series: Above 0.2: 81%, Above 0.5: 63%, Above 0.7: 58%, Above 1.0: 51%, Above 1.1: 12%. The ladder is not internally consistent: Above 1.2 is 1% while Above 1.3 is 4%. The market implies a median headline print of about 1.0%, so it expects more energy-led strength.
- Kalshi PPI year-over-year for October: median about 6.6%, with Above 6.3 at 74%. That compares with 6.3% in September.
- Polymarket year-over-year: there is little liquidity in the 6.4% and lower buckets, at about 3-4% each.
- Kalshi core CPI for October: 0.2 at 41%, 0.3 at 38%. That points to moderate consumer core inflation.
- I found no Kalshi or Polymarket market for this exact series.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-04/05: ISM services PMI for October, including services prices paid.
- Around 2026-11-10 to 11-12: the October CPI and import prices may come out before the PPI. I did not verify these dates.
- 2026-11-13, 8:30 ET: October PPI release, which resolves the question.
- Ongoing: Middle East supply risk, with Brent above $113, which matters for freight and transport services. Another swing factor is equity-market-driven portfolio management fees.
